Record Class HeldRecord

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
io.github.tobyjamesclements.parsley.HeldRecord
Record Components:
stage - the stage whose task holds the record
taskId - the task, as Kafka Streams names it
topic - the source topic the held record arrived on
partition - its partition, which is the task's own
offset - the held record's offset
queueDepth - how many records wait on this channel, the head included
heldMs - milliseconds this record has been its channel's head, measured from the first sample that observed it there — a restored hold ages from the restart, not from its original arrival
unmet - the causes still missing; never empty, since a record with nothing unmet is delivered rather than held
public record HeldRecord(String stage, String taskId, String topic, int partition, long offset, int queueDepth, long heldMs, List<HeldRecord.Unmet> unmet) extends Record
Why one record is waiting at the causal gate: the record's coordinate, how long it has gated its channel, and the causes it is still waiting for. Obtained from CausalStreams.explainHolds() and, for holds that outlive their stage's holdWarningAfter threshold, written to the log.

Only the head of a channel's hold queue appears here. Holding is head-of-line blocking by design, so the head is the whole story: everything behind it on that channel waits on it, not on causes of its own.

This is a diagnostic observation, not a query surface. It carries coordinates, claims, and local watermarks — never key or value bytes, on the same principle that keeps payloads out of the log — and it describes the task's in-flight view at the moment it was sampled, which an aborted transaction may roll back. Read it to find out why a record is waiting; read sinks for what the application computed.

The rule this exists to serve: a held record is the gate doing its job. The fix is always to deliver the missing cause, never to skip, reorder, or time out — see docs/guide/diagnosing-holds.md.
